text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

-- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said yesterday that a clear-cut statement must be made at the NATO summit in Madrid that the expansion of the alliance will continue, and those states not admitted in the first round must receive a clear signal about what to do to gain membership.

-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad declared yesterday that his country wants to benefit from Hungarian experience and institutional and personal contacts in the former Yugoslavia in working to re-establish a communications and transport network there.

-- Opposition Smallholder's Party President Jozsef Torgyan yesterday declared that his party is breaking off any official links with the Free Democrats as long as Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze is president of the party, and the interior minister is delegated by the Free Democrats.

-- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny announced Monday that his ministry is suing the Health Insurance Authority (OEO) regarding irregularities in the Authority's purchase of a Wesselenyi utca property in Budapest.
-- Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha told Parliament yesterday that the privatization law must be amended because the process is drawing to a close.

-- The president of the Hungarian Energy Office announced Monday that the consumer price of natural gas will go up by 11.3%, (that of household rates by 9.9%) and the electricity rate by 4.5% as of July 1.

-- The secretariat of the Budapest Stock Exchange suspended trading of Pick shares for one day yesterday. The move was prompted by news item in Monday's Nepszabadsag, according to which Pick has won the tender for the meat company Ringa Rt.

-- The State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) may invite bids for Mezobank on July 1, if the government approves the plan on Thursday. The APV board of directors is expected to decide Wednesday who will be invited for the closed offering, managing director Gabor Nemeth said.
NEPSZABADSAG
-- The US investment bank Salomon Brothers has issued a 'hold' recommendation for MOL shares, after a recent evaluation of the state oil and gas company.
-- The state privatisation agency APV board of directors has decided to sell 45% of the Vac-based photochemical company Forte Fotokemiai Rt. for compensation coupons.
NEPSZAVA

-- Nepszava reports that the national disciplinary and ethics committee of the opposition Christian Democratic Party may take action against parliamentary group leader Tamas Isepy regarding his public questioning of the validity of party president Gyorgy Giczy's re-election on Saturday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
-- Romanian army Chief of Staff Constantin Degeratu is to hold talks with his Hungarian counterpart Ferenc Vegh in Budapest on establishing a proposed Hungarian-Romanian peacekeeping battalion.
-- Preliminary reports reveal that Postabank shareholders are willing to stump up more than the minimum Ft 5 billion requested in a closed capital increase expected to close today.
NAPI GAZDASAG

-- A road and rail corridor though Hungary was yesterday classified as part of EU corridor 5, and therefore eligible for EU financial support, Transport, Telecoms and Water Minister Karoly Lotz told Napi Gazdasag. The decision was made at the ongoing European transport conference in Helsinki.
